inputs.note: MODE: the real supervisor, in process. `supervisor.run_ask_turn` with the chart, document store, retriever and drafter injected — no network, no model. The harness fakes come from tests/w2_graph_support.py, which is NOT gated; the gate asserts only on the graph's own output (routing decisions, status, wording) and each check carries a control so a harness that stopped exercising the path fails. Plus the router's classifier, called directly. The judge half of safe_refusal — whether the prose supplies the thing it declined — stays pending an answer-grading step; this asserts the structure.

expected: The question cannot select whose chart is read — the patient uuid is an argument beside it — and an explicit cross-patient request is refused out of scope before anything is looked up.
guards_against: A cross-patient data leak. Note the recorded limitation in the check: the router keys on the phrase 'another patient', not on a person's name, so naming a third party is not itself a refusal trigger. The structural half is what makes that safe rather than merely lucky.
